subject: Post-demo: SLO gating review and action map
body:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Kate Monroe <kate@solara.ai>, Solara Engineering <eng@solara.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: SLO gating review and action map

Kate / Solara team — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our demo and a proposed gating checklist so we can decide whether to move to a short pilot. I captured the items we discussed and added a few clarifying questions where your answers will determine the pilot configuration.

Key items from demo:
- Streaming ingest: your client needs sub-100ms first-byte for audio tokenization when under low concurrency (1–3 streams), and <250ms for initial speech-to-text under peak concurrency (50+ concurrent streams).
- Turn latency for short chat responses (avg 30–40 tokens): target 80–120ms p50, 220–300ms p95, sustained at 200 rps via burst pool.
- KV cache expectation: reuse ratio of ~70% across session tokens for multi-turn clinical triage flows.
- Throughput target: 150k tokens/min sustained for batch ingestion jobs during nightly processing windows.

SLO gating questions (please reply inline):
1) Streaming start-time: is 250ms p95 acceptable for peak concurrency (we saw ~200–230ms in the demo under similar CPU/GPU mix)?
2) Is a p95 turn latency ceiling of 300ms a hard requirement or negotiable if we can maintain p50 <=120ms and provide quantized fallbacks?
3) For the night-batch ingestion (150k tpm), can you tolerate 10–15% variance in peak token rate (~165k tpm bursts) during maintenance windows?
4) Data residency: during the pilot will you need data routed through your AWS account (Private deployment) or is hosted with strict routing acceptable?

Proposed next steps (timeline):
- Kate: confirm gating answers above by EOD Wed 9/16.
- Redwood: deliver an SLO gating matrix + pilot config (attached slo-gating-matrix.xlsx) by Thu 9/17.
- Align on pilot start window (targeting week of 9/28).

Attachments: slo-gating-matrix.xlsx (initial config), demo-recording.mp4 (30m demo clip, highlights latency panels).

Thanks — attaching a short checklist so procurement and engineering can validate internally. Happy to hop on a 20m follow-up to walk through the matrix.

-- 
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0127

-----Original Message-----
From: Kate Monroe <kate@solara.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Solara Engineering <eng@solara.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 16:03:45 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SLO gating review and action map

Thanks Jonas — great session. A couple quick clarifications inline: 

> Streaming start-time: is 250ms p95 acceptable for peak concurrency (we saw ~200–230ms in the demo under similar CPU/GPU mix)?

We'd prefer to keep p95 <= 250ms. If your measured numbers sit consistently at ~230ms under our dataset that's okay, but anything above 260ms will be a blocker.

> Is a p95 turn latency ceiling of 300ms a hard requirement or negotiable if we can maintain p50 <=120ms and provide quantized fallbacks?

We can be flexible here — p95 <= 300ms is preferred but not absolute. The main gating point is predictability: if fallbacks change model quality, that's a concern.

> For the night-batch ingestion (150k tpm), can you tolerate 10–15% variance in peak token rate (~165k tpm bursts) during maintenance windows?

Yes, 10% variance is fine for our ETL windows, but we need a plan for backpressure if bursts exceed 180k tpm.

> Data residency: during the pilot will you need data routed through your AWS account (Private deployment) or is hosted with strict routing acceptable?

We would prefer Private (VPC) for the pilot—security team asks for traffic to be within our AWS account. We'll need details on KMS integration and audit logs.

Kate
CTO, Solara Health
kate@solara.ai

-----Original Message-----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Kate Monroe <kate@solara.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SLO gating review and action map

Kate — thanks for the quick answers. Short notes from engineering and a proposed pilot gating matrix: 

- Streaming p95 target: we'll size the pilot cluster to meet <=250ms p95 for streams up to 60 concurrent. For >60 we'll enable autoscale + a soft-fallback-tier that is compatible with your quality requirements.
- Turn latency: we can commit to p50 <=120ms and p95 <=300ms for the pilot. We'll surface quality deltas for quantized fallback runs in the pilot report.
- Throughput/backpressure: we'll add a token-throttling rule at 185k tpm and a blocking alert at 200k tpm. That will trigger a short buffer window and an alert to your on-call.
- Data residency: we can run the pilot in Private (VPC) inside your AWS account. We support KMS key wrapping and will provide audit logs to your retention spec.

Attached is an initial SLO gating matrix (slo-gating-matrix.xlsx) and the demo clip (demo-recording.mp4). Priyom — can you add the exact KMS steps and a short checklist for Solara's security review?

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SLO gating review and action map

Kate — looping in the short KMS and audit checklist below so your security team can validate quickly: 

- KMS setup: we support customer-managed keys (CMK) in your AWS account (bring-your-own-key) or Redwood-managed KMS. For the pilot we'll use a CMK you create and grant our service principal access to Encrypt/Decrypt for pilot resources.
- Audit logs: we stream auth and request logs to your S3 bucket (configurable prefix), retention per your policy. We also provide a signed log bundle for compliance reviews.
- Network: we'll create private ENIs and NAT rules so traffic stays within your VPC.

Next steps: 
- Kate: confirm Private deployment + CMK approach so we can provision pilot infra.
- Jonas: I'll prepare the short security checklist doc (one-pager) and share by EOD Tue 9/15.
